What led you to the barefoot lifestyle?

For me, it started a couple of years ago, when I learned of Vibram FiveFingers and the benefits of minimalist shoes. I wore those for the better part of a year, then I discovered barefooting. I learned more about it, and saw all the scientific research backing barefooting (sorry about your lawsuit, Vibram). Finally, right near the 1-year mark, I bought a pair of Barebottom Shoes, which allowed me to go barefoot without really being barefoot. The Barebottoms worked great through the seasons, and I really enjoyed being barefoot. Recently, I passed the 1-year mark of wearing Barebottoms, and finally decided it's time to go fully barefoot! I've had few issues so far, and I expect any issues that do come up can be easily handled with the sheer amount of research and legal backing of barefooting.

Ive practiced martial arts for over 20 years, and because a lot of my formative years growing up were spent barefoot on the mats it has always felt more natural for me. I also did so much of my running on those mats early on that I naturally learned to forefoot or midfoot strike.

At one point in middle school cross country I had a coach who tried to get us all to run heel-to-toe, but that just messed me up.

A couple years ago I got back into running and discovered minimalist shoes. Started with VFF. I currently run unshod one or two times a week for shorter runs, and with Merrell Trail Gloves the other days - I have switched away from Vibrams because they have changed basically every style of shoe they make to either slip-on or quicklaces, and neither of those are comfortable for me (The old Spyridons with the velcro were the best VFF Ive ever had).

I teach martial arts full time, so I am still barefoot most of the time. I keep a pair of flip flops in my car in case I have to go into any stores, but I drive barefoot, I walk places barefoot, etc. In the winter I switch the flip fops for a pair of Sanuks.

Oh, and I ran my first 50 mile ultra in VFF.

That's cool that you have such a long history with being barefoot. I wish I had more of a basis than self-driven research, but oh well.

Yeah, sports could learn a lot from losing the one-size-fits-all approach to training. Oh, and congrats on the ultra!

Yeah, sports could learn a lot from losing the one-size-fits-all approach to training.

Definitely this. Barefoot might not be for everyone, but huge cushions on modern running shoes are not right for everyone, either. Its up to each individual to figure out what works for them, but I think that most people could benefit from at least some amount of barefoot training.

Scott Jurek talks about it in Eat & Run:

The beautiful thing about running barefoot or in minimal footwear is that you are working with your body's natural proprioception, the ability to sense your own position in space. With nothing between you and the ground, you get immediate sensory feedback with every step, which encourages you to stay light on your feet and run with proper form. Some people who are recovering from injuries or who have structural anomalies or who just like their shoes will keep lacing up. But whether you wear shoes or go barefoot, what's important is that you pay attention to your form. If running barefoot helps with that, it's beneficial.

...

Lighter weight, minimal running shoes and racing flats will give you a similar type of feel as running barefoot. It will all help you with form. I have been running most of my long training runs and ultra races in Brooks racing flats for almost a decade, even Badwater and Spartathlon. Racing flats and minimal shoes provide the best of both worlds: comfort and performance.
I used to do some tumbling on the grass bare foot... Got a wart. Couple years later a bee sting and then the pistachio shells... No barefoot for me.

The Buddha got his food either by going on alms rounds or by being invited to the houses of his supporters and in both cases he ate what he was given.
